$comment: GOLIVE-PERM-001 step 2 — which permission switch each operational endpoint reads.
Step 1 enforced the two destructive endpoints. Extending that mechanically by HTTP verb
was not possible: of the eleven POSTs under api/clinic-queue exactly one creates anything.
Call, recall, start, complete, enter-room, no-show and notify are state transitions on a
queue item that already exists. Mapping them to `create` because they are POSTs would put
'who may call the next patient' behind a switch labelled «إنشاء» on «الطابور», which is
less honest than having no switch at all.
The frontend had already invented its own mapping and contradicted itself doing so:
call -> clinic_queue.create, recall -> clinic_queue.edit, enter-room -> clinic_queue.approve.
So the mapping is written down deliberately, once, here, and both sides read it.
The action vocabulary is fixed at the six columns on RolePermission (view/create/edit/
delete/export/approve). Adding verbs like 'call' would need a schema migration; it is not
worth one. State transitions therefore map to `edit` — they mutate an existing row — and
`enforced: false` means the endpoint is listed and agreed but the guard is not switched on
yet, because turning it on would remove an ability a role uses today. Those await the
owner's role-by-role review; the impact per role is in docs/audits/.

endpoints.note: Step 1. Reception with the switch off deleted an appointment and got 200.
Step 1. Checked after CLIN-01's per-patient check so its message survives.
The only genuine create under this route.
Admits an appointment into the queue — creates the queue item.
The one destructive transition — withholding it is the point of a separate switch.
Reception edited a patient with patients.edit off and got 200. Correcting a phone number is normal reception work, so the seed is the likelier defect, not the call.
All three doctor roles are seeded visits.edit=false yet may reach this. A doctor who cannot edit their own visit note is a seed defect, not a policy.

notEnforceableByDesign.reason: Only Admin reaches DELETE /api/patients/{id}, and PermissionGuard bypasses Admin, so the switch can never change the outcome. Left visible rather than removed, but it decides nothing.
